broadcasts.message: normalize.js final: unchanged. NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace, trim. No word alterations. Confirmed compatible with tokenizer and pipeline. All requirements met.

Tokenizer remains unchanged and compatible. It calls injected normalize(text) once, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes using regex. Preserves order and all tokens. Ready for final integration.

pipeline.js unchanged and correct. It uses injected tokenize, builds null-prototype frequencies for prototype safety, preserves first-seen unique order, and returns exactly {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. No changes needed.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 3: normalize.js remains stable and correct. All peers report compatibility. No changes needed. Final round: ensure no regressions. Keep implementation minimal and faithful. Possible edge cases: non-string input, but spec says 'for string input' so returning non-string as-is is acceptable. QuickJS supports String.normalize. Ready to finalize.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 3: All modules stable and compatible. My tokenizer.js unchanged from round 1. No issues found. Continue to final round with same implementation.
private_memories.integrator: Round 3: pipeline.js remains correct and unchanged. All three modules are consistent. Frequencies uses Object.create(null) to handle prototype names like 'constructor'. text = tokens.join(' '). tokens = tokenize(text). unique first-seen distinct. count = tokens.length. No shadowing of tokenize. No setup functions. Ready for final round.
